66522-learning-and-other-essays.title: Other Essays
66522-learning-and-other-essays.creator: John Jay Chapman
66522-learning-and-other-essays.description: A book by John Jay Chapman. What are Art and Religion and all those higher interests in civilization which are always vaguely held up to us as being the most important things in life? These things elude definition. They cannot be put into words except through the interposition of what the Germans call ‘a metaphysic.

arxiv-2109-04529.title: Parameterized inapproximability of Morse matching
arxiv-2109-04529.creator: Ulrich Bauer, Abhishek Rathod
arxiv-2109-04529.description: Abstract We study the problem of minimizing the number of critical simplices from the point of view of inapproximability and parameterized complexity. We first show inapproximability of Min-Morse Matching within a factor of 2 log ( 1 − ϵ ) ⁡ n 2^{\log^{(1-\epsilon)}n} .

arxiv-2110-04372.title: Fair Regression under Sample Selection Bias
arxiv-2110-04372.creator: Wei Du, Xintao Wu, Hanghang Tong
arxiv-2110-04372.description: Abstract Recent research on fair regression focused on developing new fairness notions and approximation methods as target variables and even the sensitive attribute are continuous in the regression setting. However, all previous fair regression research assumed the training data and testing data are drawn from the same distributions.

arxiv-2212-09969.title: Multiple Testing in Genome-Wide Association Studies via Hierarchical Hidden Markov Models
arxiv-2212-09969.creator: Pengfei Wang, Zhaofeng Tian
arxiv-2212-09969.description: Abstract The problems of large-scale multiple testing are often encountered in modern scientific researches. Conventional multiple testing procedures usually suffer considerable loss of testing efficiency due to the lack of consideration of correlations among tests. In fact, the appropriate use of correlation information not only enhances the efficacy of multiple testing but also improves the interpretability of the results.

arxiv-2407-14398.title: Exponential Quantum Advantage for Pathfinding in Regular Sunflower Graphs
arxiv-2407-14398.creator: Jianqiang Li, Yu Tong
arxiv-2407-14398.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Jianqiang Li, Yu Tong. Finding problems that allow for superpolynomial quantum speedup is one of the most important tasks in quantum computation. A key challenge is identifying problem structures that can only be exploited by quantum mechanics. In this paper, we find a class of graphs that allows for exponential quantum-classical separation for the pathfinding problem with the adjacency list oracle and name it the regular sunflower graph.

arxiv-2408-08976.title: Tunable Hyperuniformity in Cellular Structures
arxiv-2408-08976.creator: Yiwen Tang, Xinzhi Li, Dapeng Bi
arxiv-2408-08976.description: Abstract Hyperuniform materials, characterized by their suppressed density fluctuations and vanishing structure factors as the wave number approaches zero, represent a unique state of matter that straddles the boundary between order and randomness. These materials exhibit exceptional optical, mechanical, and acoustic properties, making them of great interest in materials science and engineering.

arxiv-2502-02887.title: Variations on the Expectation due to Changes in the Probability Measure Thanks: This work is supported in part by the European Commission through the H2020-MSCA-RISE-2019 project 872172; the French National Agency for Research (ANR) through the Project ANR-21-CE25-0013 and the project ANR-22-PEFT-00
arxiv-2502-02887.creator: Samir M. Perlaza 1 2 3 and Gaetan Bisson 3
arxiv-2502-02887.description: Abstract In this paper, closed-form expressions are presented for the variation of the expectation of a given function due to changes in the probability measure used for the expectation. They unveil interesting connections with Gibbs probability measures, mutual information, and lautum information.

arxiv-2506-02133.title: Characterization of latency and jitter in TSN emulation
arxiv-2506-02133.creator: Álex Gracia, José Luis Briz, Héctor Blanco-Alcaine, Juan Segarra, Alitzel G. Torres-Macías 1,, Antonio Ramírez-Treviño
arxiv-2506-02133.description: Abstract This research focuses on timestamping methods for profiling network traffic in software-based environments. Accurate timestamping is crucial for evaluating network performance, particularly in Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN). We explore and compare four timestamping techniques within a TSN emulation context, though its findings extend to other network scenarios.

arxiv-2511-00346.title: Exploiting Latent Space Discontinuities for Building Universal LLM Jailbreaks and Data Extraction Attacks
arxiv-2511-00346.creator: Kayuã Oleques Paim, Rodrigo Brandão Mansilha, Diego Kreutz, Muriel Figueredo Franco, Weverton Cordeiro
arxiv-2511-00346.description: Abstract The rapid proliferation of Large Language Models (LLMs) has raised significant concerns about their security against adversarial attacks. In this work, we propose a novel approach to crafting universal jailbreaks and data extraction attacks by exploiting latent space discontinuities, an architectural vulnerability related to the sparsity of training data.

europmc-pmc4819444.creator: Hanslmayr S, Staresina BP, Bowman H.
europmc-pmc4819444.description: Brain oscillations are one of the core mechanisms underlying episodic memory. However, while some studies highlight the role of synchronized oscillatory activity, others highlight the role of desynchronized activity. We here describe a framework to resolve this conundrum and...

pmc-10570855.title: Effects of Dextrose Supplementation on Chloral Hydrate Sedation: A Double-Blinded, Randomized, Prospective Study
pmc-10570855.creator: Young Kwon Koh, Han Gil Kang, Young Kuk Cho
pmc-10570855.description: Sedation plays a crucial role in successful pediatric imaging, and chloral hydrate is commonly used for this purpose. However, the challenges associated with chloral hydrate administration, such as its unpleasant taste and potential induction of vomiting, remain a concern. Sweet oral solutions have emerged as potential solutions for reducing distress and providing analgesia.

pmc-11434707.title: An Organic Fraction of Oenothera rosea L’Her Ex. Aiton Prevents Neuroinflammation in a Rat Ischemic Model
pmc-11434707.creator: Alejandro Costet-Mejía, Gabriela Trejo-Tapia, Itzel Isaura Baca-Ibarra, Aida Araceli Rodríguez-Hernández, Julio García-Hernández, Brenda Hildeliza Camacho-Díaz, Alejandro Zamilpa
pmc-11434707.description: Background: Oenothera rosea L’Her Ex. Aiton, presenting antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities, is traditionally used to treat bruises and headaches and as a healing agent. This study aimed to investigate whether its organic fraction (EAOr) has neuroprotective properties against neuroinflammation in the context of ischemia/reperfusion.

pmc-11774841.title: N-acetylcysteine use in a cocaine-induced liver failure: a case report
pmc-11774841.creator: Vanessa Biering, Ronan Bellouard, Maëlle Martin, Éric Dailly, Catherine Monteil-Ganière, Edouard Charles Le Carpentier
pmc-11774841.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundCocaine intoxication and abuse is a worldwide problem that can be the cause of numerous acute medical complications, including severe acute hepatitis. Although these cases are scarce, they are extremely serious and may lead to liver transplantation or death.

pmc-12467072.title: Translating Alzheimer’s Disease Mechanisms into Therapeutic Opportunities
pmc-12467072.creator: Jiejia Li, Liyun Wang, Xiaodan Zhang, Jianhua Shi, Yizhun Zhu, Han Wang, Xiangyang Zhu, Qing Zhu, Jia-Lie Luo, Fabio Di Domenico, Zhidong Zhou
pmc-12467072.description: Alzheimer’s disease (AD), characterized by progressive cognitive decline and functional impairment, is the most prevalent cause of dementia, and it poses a significant socioeconomic and caregiving burden on patients, families, and healthcare systems. Notwithstanding comprehensive research, the precise causes underlying AD remain ambiguous.

pmc-12540810.title: Cinnamaldehyde as a dietary modulator of gut microbiota and growth in broilers under low-protein feeding conditions
pmc-12540810.creator: Xinzhu Chen, Wen Yue, Zhongrong Li, Weigang Jin, Haihong Lin, Jing Liu
pmc-12540810.description: Cinnamaldehyde (CM), recognized for its antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory capabilities, is increasingly valued as an animal feed additive, primarily for its potential to augment gut health and promote general animal welfare. However, our understanding of CM as a feed additive to a low-protein diet on broilers’ growth performance and microbial composition is still limited.

pmc-12554275.title: Unveiling Psychological Capital Profiles and Their Impact on Quality of Life in Breast Cancer Patients: A Latent Profile Analysis
pmc-12554275.creator: Chunying Cui, Hairong Liu, Lie Wang
pmc-12554275.description: PurposeOur study aimed to identify the profiles of psychological capital (PsyCap), explore its influencing factors, and examine the association between PsyCap and quality of life (QoL) among breast cancer (BC) patients.MethodsA total of 229 BC patients completed our survey questionnaire.

pmc-12654483.title: Thromboembolic Risk After Total Hip Replacement Versus Hemiarthroplasty in Femoral Neck Fracture Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-12654483.creator: Ibrahim A Hakami, Mohammed A Altammar, Shafi A Alaklabi, Meshari M Alotaibi, Saleh N Almunyif, Mohammed I Alshuwaier, Sultan T Alobaysi, Sultan S Aldalbahi, Abdullah H Alotaibi, Mohammed M Alotaibi, Omar S Alobaysi, Moath T Aladhyani, Mohammad A Jareebi, Eduardo García-Rey, Alberto D Delgado-Martíne
pmc-12654483.description: Background and Objectives: Femoral neck fractures are common among elderly patients and are typically managed surgically to restore mobility and reduce complications. Total Hip Replacement (THR) and Hemiarthroplasty (HA) are standard interventions. While both procedures are widely used, the comparative risks of thromboembolic complications remain unclear.

pmc-13236741.title: Loop-mediated isothermal amplification-lateral flow dipstick (LAMP-LFD) for detection of wine microorganisms
pmc-13236741.creator: Abdul Ghani, Sergi Ferrer
pmc-13236741.description: Wine is undoubtedly one of the oldest and most celebrated beverages across cultures. It is primarily crafted from grapes through a fermentation process where yeast transforms sugars into alcohol. The presence of unwanted microorganisms can cause spoilage, so early detection of microorganisms is crucial.

pmc-13332430.title: ROS scavenging nanoengineered bioactive glass interfaces reprogram macrophage immunity for tendon–bone regeneration
pmc-13332430.creator: Bowen Cai, Fanrui Zeng, Kaixiao Xue, Zhi Shen, Chang Qiao, Han Wu, Qunyi Wang, Jue Zhang, Shahin Homaeigohar, Kai Zheng, Bin Zhu, Jiahu Fang
pmc-13332430.description: Failure of rotator cuff repair largely stems from ineffective regeneration of the tendon–bone interface (TBI), driven by persistent inflammation and excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation at the biomaterial tissue interface. Here, we engineer an immunoregulatory suture interface by incorporating cerium-doped mesoporous bioactive glass nanoparticles (Ce-MBGNs) into a gelatin/tannic acid (Gel/TA) coating on polyethylene terephthalate sutures.

pmc-13478460.title: Manganese recycling from zinc anode slime via SO2 reductive leaching in an integrated copper–zinc hydrometallurgical plant
pmc-13478460.creator: Shenghong Cheng, Shizhe Chen, Guanghua Chen, Sanping Liu, Kaixi Jiang, Bao Guo
pmc-13478460.description: Manganese is essential for zinc electrowinning but its recycling is challenging in oxide ore SX-EW circuits where P204 rejects Mn. This study proposes a novel manganese recycling strategy tailored for SX-EW streams involving the selective SO2 reductive leaching of zinc anode slime followed by impurity removal.
